Ofcom published the discussion page on 3 June 2026.
Ofcom launched a discussion paper on good mobile connectivity.
Ofcom states current UK mobile connectivity is too often not good enough.
Better mobile connectivity is linked to economic growth.
Better mobile connectivity is linked to digital inclusion.
The paper distinguishes coverage from good, reliable connectivity.
The paper describes why current provision falls short.
The paper considers recent market changes.
The paper identifies areas where further action may be needed.
Ofcom says a national effort is required.
Industry is identified as a necessary participant.
Government is identified as a necessary participant.
Local authorities and landlords are identified as participants.
Stakeholder responses will inform Ofcom's priorities.
Ofcom plans an update in early 2027.
The response deadline is 5pm on 29 July 2026.
The page links qualitative research on consumer mobile-quality experiences.
The page links a Greater Manchester connectivity report.
The page links a connectivity-on-trains measurement study.

The Shared Rural Network agreement involves four mobile network operators.
Each operator committed to 88% UK landmass coverage by 30 June 2024.
The updated agreement targets 89.2% UK landmass by 31 January 2027.
Coverage obligations are implemented through varied spectrum licences.
Nation-specific thresholds apply for 2024 and 2027.
England's 2024 requirement for EE was 93%.
England's 2024 requirement for Three was 91%.
England's 2024 requirement for O2 was 92%.
England's 2024 requirement for Vodafone was 92%.
England's 2027 requirement for EE is 94%.
England's 2027 requirement for Three is 91%.
England's 2027 requirement for O2 is 93%.
England's 2027 requirement for Vodafone is 92%.
Ofcom monitors delivery of the coverage obligations.
